claims.claim: Recent US high-voltage transmission projects cost on the order of one to several million dollars per mile (HVDC projects reviewed by EIA ran $1.17M-$8.62M per mile).
claims.episode_span: A new high-voltage transmission line in the United States today can cost several million dollars per mile even though the copper, aluminum, and steel inside it represent only a modest fraction of that total.
claims.source_title: EIA study examines the role of high-voltage power lines in integrating renewables - Today in Energy
claims.supporting_quote: The per-mile cost of HVDC projects ranges between $1.17 million and $8.62 million, according to a review of recent proposals and relevant regulatory filings.

claims.claim: Converter stations can account for as much as 60% of the total fixed cost of an HVDC project, which is why their cost curve dominates HVDC economics.
claims.episode_span: provided converter stations themselves move down their own cost curve through modular designs
claims.source_title: EIA study examines the role of high-voltage power lines in integrating renewables - Today in Energy
claims.supporting_quote: The cost of converter stations, which can account for as much as 60% of the total fixed cost for an HVDC project, is a major cost item considered in HVDC deployment.

claims.claim: Transmission-scale transformers are engineered to order with lead times now measured in years (three to six years per Hitachi Energy).
claims.episode_span: Transformers and substations follow the same pattern; most units are engineered to order, with lead times measured in years because manufacturing capacity itself is allocated through long-term utility contracts.
claims.source_title: Transformer supply bottleneck threatens power system stability as load grows - Utility Dive
claims.supporting_quote: “Transmission scale unit lead times are now three years to six years, with specialized transformers taking the longest time,” he added.

claims.claim: Time spent in US interconnection queues has roughly doubled: median duration from interconnection request to commercial operation rose from under 2 years (projects built 2000-2007) to over 4 years (projects built 2018-2024).
claims.episode_span: Interconnection queues add another layer. A generator seeking to connect must study impacts on every neighboring line and substation
claims.source_title: Report Details Projects Looking to Interconnect to the Grid as of the End of 2024 - American Public Power Association
claims.supporting_quote: The time projects spend in queues before reaching COD is increasing. For the regions with available data, the median duration from IR to COD has doubled from <2 years for projects built in 2000-2007 to over 4 years for those built in 2018-2024.

claims.claim: Generators seeking transmission interconnection must undergo a series of grid impact studies, which establish and assign the cost of required upgrades before the project can connect.
claims.episode_span: A generator seeking to connect must study impacts on every neighboring line and substation, then fund upgrades whose scope and cost are negotiated case by case.
claims.source_title: Report Details Projects Looking to Interconnect to the Grid as of the End of 2024 - American Public Power Association
claims.supporting_quote: Electric transmission system operators require proposed power plants seeking to connect to the transmission grid to undergo a series of impact studies before they can be built
